evidence.quote: PerfOrch works at the function level, matching the scope of all four benchmarks. Section 7.6 sets out what integration with a repository-level pipeline would require.
Our four benchmarks may not cover all real-world coding scenarios.
PerfOrch requires test cases to validate generated code at each pipeline stage.
Memory would need to be re-profiled under the chosen sampling configuration, and evaluating this allocation remains future work.
Assigning labels at inference time without reference patches, profiling candidate models on these categories, and evaluating category-aware routing remain future work.
As LLMs continue to improve, HumanEval-X may eventually become too easy to tell models apart.
Noisy measurements here could lead to suboptimal model selection, causing more retry iterations and higher token cost.
Category labels also guide model selection, so incorrect labels can affect the order in which models are tried.
Measurement noise here could cause the agent to accept a slower solution or reject a faster one, resulting in non-optimized or even degraded performance.
LLM capabilities evolve rapidly, so these rankings are a snapshot.
A single re-profiling per version update is manageable, but with five model families releasing updates on different schedules, repeated full re-profiling becomes expensive.
PerfOrch solves the vast majority of problems, but some remain unsolved after multi-model orchestration.

The failure analysis in Section 5.2 marks two boundaries of the current approach: specification misunderstandings shared by every candidate model, and problems whose correct algorithm lies beyond the reach of iterative debugging.
PerfOrch would also need executable tests during candidate selection, so integration must make the host's tests available at that point.
Section 7.6 identifies the point inside a repository-level pipeline where it would attach and the conditions that integration would have to meet.
